# Clinical Metrics

This folder groups clinical metrics used to assess patient risk profiles and postoperative care quality in the Danish Acute Surgery Database. It covers comorbidity scoring systems—specifically the Charlson Comorbidity Index and its mortality strata—as well as nutritional interventions aimed at reducing postoperative complications and length of stay. Together, these metrics provide essential context for risk-adjusting surgical outcomes and evaluating adherence to evidence-based clinical quality indicators.

## Pages

- [[charlson-score|Charlson Score]] — Details the use of the Charlson Score for risk adjustment and 30-day mortality stratification, including audit recommendations and data quality concerns regarding the "score 0" population.
- [[ernaering|ernæring]] — Covers Indikator 7 on nutrition, summarizing evidence that early enteral and parenteral nutrition reduces postoperative complications and mortality after acute abdominal surgery.
- [[topics/clinical-metrics/comorbidity/index|Comorbidity]] — Groups specific strata of the Charlson Comorbidity Index used to evaluate 30-day mortality following acute surgery, isolating patient outcomes based on their comorbidity burden.
- [[topics/clinical-metrics/comorbidity-scoring/index|Comorbidity Scoring]] — Contains documentation on comorbidity scoring systems, detailing how the Charlson Comorbidity Index is calculated from a 10-year diagnostic history and applied to stratify patients.
